title: Predictive Priority Engine and Commit-Window Suggester for Escalated Accounts
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build an automated prioritization assistant that combines contractual KPIs, live usage telemetry, and escalation context to surface a ranked list of top-account asks and recommended sprint commit windows (a suggested earliest sprint and a confidence interval). This ticket scopes the MVP scoring model, UX for PM console suggestions, and a 6-week pilot with two enterprise customers.
background: We currently rely on manual scoring during weekly intake reviews for top accounts. That process is labor-intensive, inconsistent across reviewers, and often leads to blurred expectations on delivery timing. Several enterprise customers have escalated feature asks where the lack of a data-backed commit window caused friction. The goal is to reduce subjective decisions and speed up negotiation with a deterministic, auditable signal set.
proposal:
- Create a weighted scoring engine that ingests: contract SLA/KPI severity (renewal risk), multi-week usage deltas (API QPS, error rate, token spend), recent support/incident tickets, strategic signals (deal size, exec sponsor), and explicit customer urgency field.
- Output: normalized priority score (0-100), suggested commit window (Earliest Sprint + Confidence band), and rationale tokens (top 3 contributing signals).
- Surface suggestions in the PM Console intake panel and generate an optional templated response for CSMs.
- Pilot with two top accounts and measure alignment with negotiation outcome and perceived clarity.
- Limit scope: no automated changes to roadmap; suggestions only. No RBAC changes in MVP.
acceptance_criteria: Scoring engine ingests contract KPI signal, usage telemetry (last 28 days), and support ticket count and produces a score for test dataset with documented mapping.
PM Console shows the suggested commit window (earliest sprint and 1-2 sprint confidence band) alongside the score and textual rationale.
Pilot run completed with 2 customers and a post-pilot survey showing >= 60% of participants found the suggested window helpful (n>=5 stakeholders).
Telemetry and scoring logs are recorded for audit and can be exported as CSV for review.
No production changes to roadmap allocation are performed automatically during the pilot.
